common_name: October Magic Ruby Camellia (Deep Red Compact Reblooming Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; October Magic Ruby's compact, dense habit fits a smaller foundation bed better than many older, larger sasanqua cultivars.

directions: October Magic Ruby is a Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua selected for deep ruby-red, semi-double flowers on a compact, well-branched shrub that blooms more heavily and over a longer window in fall than many older sasanqua cultivars. Its saturated red color and glossy, dark evergreen foliage make it a strong focal point in a partly shaded bed during the cool season, when few other shrubs are flowering. Like other camellias it needs consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil and a layer of mulch to protect its shallow roots; prune, if needed, only lightly right after flowering to avoid removing next season's buds.

directions: October Magic Orchid is a Southern Living Plant Collection sasanqua bearing ruffled, orchid-form, soft pink flowers with wavy, slightly curled petals, a distinctive bloom shape among sasanqua camellias, on a compact, well-branched shrub that flowers heavily through the fall. common_name: Fairy Blush Camellia (Small-Flowered Pale Pink Compact Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Fairy Blush's fine texture and compact size suit it to a smaller bed, low hedge, or mass planting where a large camellia would be out of scale.

directions: Fairy Blush produces an abundance of small, single, pale pink flowers with a delicate blush deepening toward the petal edges, held above fine-textured, small, glossy evergreen leaves quite different from the larger, coarser foliage of many camellia cultivars. Its dainty flower form and dense, twiggy growth make it useful as a low informal hedge or mass planting where the sheer quantity of small blooms creates a soft haze of color through the bloom season. Like other camellias it needs consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil and a layer of mulch to protect its shallow roots; prune, if needed, only lightly right after flowering to avoid removing next season's buds.

common_name: Sweet Emily Kate Camellia (Ruffled Deep Pink Compact Sasanqua)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5-6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Sweet Emily Kate's compact, columnar-to-rounded habit fits a narrower planting space than many spreading sasanqua cultivars.

directions: Sweet Emily Kate carries ruffled, deep rose-pink, semi-double to double flowers with a distinctive curled petal texture, held on a compact, upright, well-branched sasanqua shrub that blooms heavily through the fall. Its narrower growth habit than many older sasanqua cultivars makes it a good fit for a tighter foundation planting or narrow side-yard bed, and its rich, ruffled flower color provides strong seasonal interest during a season when few other shrubs are flowering. Like other camellias it needs consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil and a layer of mulch to protect its shallow roots; prune, if needed, only lightly right after flowering to avoid removing next season's buds.
